findings.where: REPORT.md s1 item 5 and s8 (and the same text in report.typ / report.pdf)
findings.claim: 'H-M ...: INCONCLUSIVE. ic is significant (Holm, alpha 0.05) on 5 of 12 chosen curves ... IC's model dependence is therefore present on some curves and absent on others: it is neither a general property nor noise.' and s8 'With 5 of 12 the verdict is inconclusive by the plan's rule, which needed 6.'
findings.evidence: The verdict turns on one curve that sits on the Monte Carlo boundary. V6:98 ic: F = 2.8133 (validator 2.8133, equal to 1e-15); it is the 6th-smallest p of 12, so its Holm multiplier is 7. Producer, 10,000 shuffles: p = 0.0073, Holm 0.0511 -> not significant -> 5 of 12 -> 'inconclusive'. Validator, independent code, same frozen seed (20261024) and count (10,000), different draw order: p = 0.0064, Holm 0.0448 -> significant -> 6 of 12 with rho-neg 0 and bsgs 0, which the frozen rule (ANALYSIS_PLAN s5c) reads as 'supported for IC'. The same test evaluated to high precision (validation/hm_precise.py, 2,000,000 shuffles): p = 0.007111 +- 0.000059 (MC SE), Holm 0.0498 +- 0.0004 -> 6 of 12; the parametric one-way ANOVA F(7, 504) gives p = 0.00699, Holm 0.0489 -> 6 of 12. Both 10,000-shuffle Holm values agree within Monte Carlo error (the numbers are not wrong); the categorical verdict does not reproduce. The report states 'inconclusive' as a settled outcome and interprets it ('absent on others', 'neither a general property nor noise'); a curve that is not significant after Holm is not shown to lack a model effect, and the five-versus-six split is within Monte Carlo noise of the frozen threshold.
findings.fix: Erratum (a new AMENDMENTS record, REPORT.md and report.pdf; the frozen rule, seed and shuffle count are not changed): report the frozen-seed count (5 of 12, inconclusive) together with the fact that the 6th curve (V6:98, Holm p 0.0511) lies within Monte Carlo error of 0.05 and that a precise evaluation of the same permutation test (and the parametric F test) gives 6 of 12, which the rule reads as supported for IC; state that the H-M verdict is on the boundary between 'inconclusive' and 'supported for IC' and is not robust either way; withdraw 'absent on others' and 'neither a general property nor noise'. The figure 8 caption / s8 table can keep the frozen-seed values.

findings.claim: 'No variance-ratio test is significant and no curve is flagged: no V6 curve differs from its own isomorphic re-scalings beyond the control spread'
findings.evidence: With 648 curves and the pooled-|z*| reference of s4 (3 label outcomes per vertex) the smallest attainable p_v is about 1/1944 and the smallest attainable Holm-adjusted p about 648/1944 = 0.33, so no curve can reach adj. p < 0.01 whatever the data. results.json: the most extreme rho-neg curve (vertex 545, level 4, z = 5.12) has Holm p 0.331. 'No curve is flagged' is true but uninformative; the claim about curves rests on the aggregate F tests (p 0.15 / 0.67 / 0.42), which do support 'no curve effect beyond the control spread' in aggregate. The design is frozen (and is the census's).
findings.fix: Say that the per-curve flag cannot fire at this size and that the statement rests on the F test.

findings.where: REPORT.md s4 (V5 bsgs and bsgs-neg rows) and s1 item 3
findings.claim: V5 bsgs R(L) = 0.988 and bsgs-neg R(L) = 0.982 at every level 1-6, listed without comment.
findings.evidence: A constant ratio at every level is a family-mix artifact, not a level effect: Ua and Ub have no V5 level-0 rows, so the crater mean is D + N while every other level is D + Ua + Ub + N; BSGS cost depends only on k, D/Ua/Ub share k (target seed 20261123) and N has its own (20261125), with mean S(N)/S(D) = 1.0484 (bsgs) and 1.0753 (bsgs-neg). (3 + x) / (2 (1 + x)) = 0.98819 and 0.98186 reproduce the constants exactly. The same mix difference enters every V5 arm's R(L) (negligibly for rho and ic). The census validation flagged the same pattern (census F8).

findings.text: The percentile bootstrap CI of the max/min of 8 model means is biased upward and does not cover the point estimate when there is no effect (bsgs, whose model means are identical: 1.000 with CI [1.03, 1.11]; rho-neg V6:2: 1.10 [1.11, 1.38]). These CIs cannot be read against 1; IC's max/min (1.12-1.58) must be read against rho-neg's on the same curves (1.10-1.26), the null object, as the report's sentence on rho-neg partly does.

The frozen plan names the benchmarks copy benchmarks/20261023-volcano-ecdlp-census-followup/; the copy is in benchmarks/20261023-volcano-census-followup/ (the directory this validation writes to). Contents identical to research/.../report.pdf and analysis/figures (sha256 checked).

The vertex-weighted pooling (A3.2) gives T = 0.5946 / 0.5781 (0 / 1 GAE); the row-pooled alternative gives 0.6000 / 0.5831. The verdict (supported) does not depend on the choice; the T0 control's 95% CI includes 1 at all three prices with its upper end about 0.014 above 1, many Monte Carlo SE away.

limitations: Replay (ecbench verify --replay-all) covers 19 of 147 sessions (seeded stratified sample: every volcano x family stratum, the three V5 crater rho-cubic sessions, 3 Tcr, 2 M and one redone .r2 session); the other sessions rest on their Phase B audits (12 replays each, 1,764 identical) and on the validator's raw-record re-derivation, which covers all 147 archives ([k]G = Q with independent arithmetic, S, uncharged counts, extracts row by row).

The replay used the same shared cloud VM type and the same ecbench binary as the sessions; it is an independent re-execution of operation counts, not an independent solver implementation or independent hardware.

Bootstrap CIs and permutation p-values were recomputed with independent generators: they agree within Monte Carlo error, not bit for bit; verdicts that sit within about 2 Monte Carlo SE of a threshold (F1, F2) can differ between implementations.

Not re-run: the s5 transport-then-solve and paired-source bootstrap CIs and signal flags (all 100 point ratios and native controls recomputed exactly), per-vertex H-T CIs and the V5 per-family R(L); the s4 per-curve p-values were computed from the exact three-outcome reference distribution instead of 10,000 label shuffles; the s3 mixed model was re-run with the same library (statsmodels) for ic and rho-neg only.
Wall-time results are descriptive in the study and were checked only as A/A ratios and L2 fractions.
This validation does not support an ECDLP claim, a speedup, or promotion; a pass would make the receipts admissible evidence for the benchmarks row only.
